title: Placebos work even when you know

lines.text: What if a sugar pill worked, even when you knew it was a sugar pill?
In 2010, Harvard researcher Ted Kaptchuk tested exactly that.
80 people with irritable bowel syndrome took part.
Half got pills in a bottle clearly labelled placebo, and were told they contained nothing active.
The other half got no pills at all.
After three weeks, the placebo group reported significantly better improvement in their symptoms.
They didn't have to believe in it. They just had to take the pills.
Scientists are still working out why. The ritual of treatment may matter more than we think.

sources.claim: Kaptchuk et al. (PLoS ONE, 2010): 80 IBS patients; open-label placebo vs no treatment; significantly better global improvement at 11 and 21 days

publish.title: Placebos Work Even When You KNOW It's a Placebo 💊
